title: About Polaris Astro Controller
lede: Polaris Astro Controller is a self-hosted, browser-based astrophotography control, capture and processing suite. It runs entirely on your own device (a Raspberry Pi, mini PC, or computer) and is reached from any browser on your network, with no app to install on the viewing device. It controls your equipment (INDI, ASCOM, Alpaca, and native camera SDKs), runs live stacking, guiding, focusing, plate solving, and sequencing, and includes a full editor with AI background extraction, denoise, and deconvolution.

author.title: Author & contact
author.name: Daniel Wagner Oliveira de Medeiros
bio: Daniel is a chemical engineer (UFRN, Brazil) and an experienced software developer with 21+ years of experience. He designs and ships production software across Windows Desktop, Linux and macOS, on mobile (Android and iOS with Xamarin), and increasingly with on-device AI.

His main project is DWSIM, a free, open-source, CAPE-OPEN-compliant chemical process simulator he has developed since 2008. DWSIM models entire chemical plants: rigorous thermodynamics and phase equilibria, dozens of unit operations, petroleum characterization and dynamic simulation, running on Windows, Linux, macOS and even Android and iOS. It is used worldwide by students, universities and process engineers as an open alternative to commercial simulators, and it won the 2012 CAPE-OPEN Award.

Polaris Astro Controller brings that same engineering discipline to astrophotography: real numerical and scientific code, from astrometry, guiding and plate solving to image stacking, colour calibration and on-device AI, built to run reliably on hardware as small as a Raspberry Pi. It is where two decades of software engineering meet a lifelong pull toward the night sky.

version.title: Version & source
version.body: Polaris ships frequent releases. The current code, the latest build, and the release notes all live on the project page on GitHub. On a .deb install, Polaris can update itself with one click from the status bar.

report.title: Report a problem
report.body: Found a bug, or have a feature request? Open an issue or start a discussion on GitHub. The in-app reporter pre-fills your client and server details to make diagnosis easier.

support.title: Support the project
support.body: Polaris stays free and open-source. If it has saved you an evening of fiddling and you would like to chip in, support is welcome but entirely optional. You can also follow development news and join the community.

credits.title: Credits & acknowledgements
credits.intro: Polaris Astro Controller stands on the shoulders of a large community of astronomy and open-source projects. Some we derive code from, some we studied as a reference, and many ship inside the capture and processing stack. Thank you to every author below. Full license texts are bundled with the app and in the source repository.

items.name: N.I.N.A. - Nighttime Imaging 'N' Astronomy
items.note: Stefan Berg and the N.I.N.A. contributors. Polaris is derived from N.I.N.A.; large parts of the imaging, astrometry, sequencer and equipment model originate here (MPL-2.0).

items.name: PHD2 - Open PHD Guiding
items.note: Andy Galasso, Bret McKee, Craig Stark and the PHD2 contributors. Used both as the managed external guider and as the reference for the built-in native autoguider and the gear simulator (BSD-3-Clause).

items.name: GraXpert
items.note: the GraXpert development team. Background extraction, denoising and deconvolution ONNX models, and the auto-stretch algorithm Polaris uses by default.

items.name: nox
items.note: charvey2718. StarNet-like star-removal model (native colour and gray), the default behind Remove stars in FILES. Code and weights MIT.

items.name: starrem2k13
items.note: code2k13. pix2pix-style U-Net star-removal model, an alternative in Remove stars. Code and weights MIT.

items.name: StarNet++
items.note: Nikita Misiura (nekitmm). The original star-removal neural network, available in Remove stars. Code MIT; pre-trained weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (NonCommercial).

items.name: Siril
items.note: the Free-Astro / Siril team. Optional external pre-processing and stacking integration.

items.name: ASTAP
items.note: Han Kleijn. The default fast offline plate solver and star database.

items.name: Astrometry.net
items.note: Dustin Lang, David W. Hogg and collaborators. Local and online blind plate solving.

items.name: PlateSolve3
items.note: PlaneWave Instruments. Alternative plate solver.

items.name: INDI Library
items.note: Jasem Mutlaq and the INDI community. The primary equipment-control protocol (400+ Linux drivers).

items.name: ASCOM Initiative & Alpaca
items.note: the ASCOM Initiative. Windows COM drivers and the cross-platform Alpaca protocol.

items.name: ZWO ASI SDK
items.note: Suzhou ZWO Co., Ltd. Native ZWO camera support.

items.name: SVBony SDK
items.note: SVBONY. Native SVBony camera support.

items.name: Player One SDK
items.note: Player One Astronomy. Native Player One camera support.

items.name: ToupTek SDK
items.note: ToupTek Astro. Native ToupTek (and OEM-alike) camera support.

items.name: Nikon SDK
items.note: Nikon Corporation. Nikon DSLR / mirrorless support.

items.name: Canon EDSDK
items.note: Canon Inc. Canon EOS DSLR / mirrorless support on Windows.

items.name: Sony Camera Remote SDK
items.note: Sony Corporation. Sony Alpha camera support on Windows.

items.name: libgphoto2 / gPhoto2
items.note: the gPhoto team. DSLR / mirrorless support on Linux, via the INDI gphoto driver.

items.name: OpenNGC
items.note: Mattia Verga. The bundled NGC/IC/Messier/Caldwell deep-sky catalog (CC BY-SA 4.0).

items.name: APASS - AAVSO Photometric All-Sky Survey
items.note: the AAVSO. Reference photometry for color calibration.

items.name: Aladin Lite
items.note: CDS, Université de Strasbourg / CNRS. The interactive sky atlas viewer.

items.name: Stellarium Web Engine
items.note: Stellarium Labs / Guillaume Chéreau and contributors. The WebGL planetarium sky view (AGPL-3.0).

items.name: Astronomy Engine
items.note: Don Cross. High-precision ephemeris and coordinate math.

items.name: Alpine.js
items.note: Caleb Porzio and contributors. The reactive framework behind the web UI.

items.name: Chart.js
items.note: the Chart.js contributors. Focus / guiding / statistics charts.

items.name: OpenSeadragon
items.note: the OpenSeadragon contributors. Deep-zoom image viewer.

items.name: noVNC
items.note: the noVNC authors. The embedded PHD2 GUI on Windows (MPL-2.0).

items.name: xterm.js
items.note: the xterm.js authors. In-browser terminal.

items.name: SunCalc
items.note: Vladimir Agafonkin. Sun / twilight calculations for the sky view.

items.name: SortableJS
items.note: the SortableJS contributors. Drag-and-drop in the sequencer.

items.name: Silk.NET
items.note: the .NET Foundation. OpenCL bindings for the optional SBC GPU compute backend.

items.name: SkiaSharp
items.note: Microsoft, wrapping Google's Skia. Server-side image encoding and rendering.

items.name: LibRaw
items.note: the LibRaw authors (LGPL-2.1 / CDDL). Optional system shared library, loaded at runtime to decode DSLR/mirrorless RAW (CR2/NEF/ARW) into real 16-bit linear data for the live stack.

items.name: ONNX Runtime (Web)
items.note: Microsoft. Runs the GraXpert AI models in the browser.

items.name: YARP
items.note: Microsoft. Reverse proxy for the embedded device web UIs.

items.name: .NET Community Toolkit (MVVM)
items.note: the .NET Foundation.

items.name: K4os.Compression.LZ4
items.note: Milosz Krajewski. Fast frame compression for the live preview.

items.name: LettuceEncrypt
items.note: Nate McMaster. Automatic Let's Encrypt certificates.

items.name: Serilog
items.note: the Serilog contributors. Structured logging.

items.name: Json.NET
items.note: James Newton-King. JSON serialization.

items.name: SSH.NET
items.note: the SSH.NET contributors.

items.name: SMBLibrary
items.note: Tal Aloni. Pure-managed SMB1/SMB2 client for the auto-push-to-network-storage backend.

items.name: net-mdns (Makaretu.Dns)
items.note: Richard Schneider. The nina.local mDNS discovery.

items.name: SQLite
items.note: D. Richard Hipp and the SQLite team. On-device databases.

items.name: Rockchip RKNN runtime
items.note: Rockchip. Optional NPU acceleration for AI models on RK35xx boards.

credits.outro: Plus the wider amateur astronomy and free-software communities whose tools, drivers, documentation and feedback make a project like this possible. If your work is used here and not listed, it is an oversight, not an intent; please let us know on GitHub.
